decisions.id: T168-1 retask mode of the existing refile
decisions.summary: Re-tasking is a new --retask / RETASK= mode of make events-refile (refile/retask.rs, called from refile::cli_in), not a new tool.
decisions.why: Serves the request's per-task breakdown ('for each task ... where our time went', 2026-11-19) and the tooling question's 'no new tool to learn' (the approved proposal); correcting misbooked lines is what makes FR-005's per-task columns and SC-002 true for 449. Placement in the existing command narrows nothing.

decisions.id: T168-2 the brief's task via the shared reader
decisions.summary: The feature and task a session is re-booked to come from set_down_hooks::page_session_brief (T161), the same reader the writer uses.
decisions.why: An implementation choice that keeps the correction and the writer (T167) agreeing; nothing asked is narrowed.

decisions.id: T168-3 idempotent, DRY=1, write_back, unlisted and task-less sessions reported and left
decisions.summary: A line already on its brief's task is not rewritten; DRY=1 writes nothing; the rewrite uses refile's write_back to keep lines a live hook appends; a session not in the index or whose brief names no task is reported and left.
decisions.why: Safety properties of a rewrite of a live log. Leaving a session whose brief names no task is not a carve-out: there is no task to book it to, and it is reported, not silently dropped.

decisions.id: T168-4 2647 and f1d2 book to T333, not T330
decisions.summary: Two of the three sessions the observation calls T330's are booked to T333 because their briefs' first lines name T333.
decisions.why: The direct consequence of the stated rule (minutes credited to the task the brief names), measured from the briefs' first lines; it applies the rule rather than excepting a case from it.

decisions.id: T168-5 where-time's first table T330 row stays 0
decisions.summary: After the re-booking, the agents table credits T330 (180 agents, 76.2 agent minutes) and T333; the first table's T330 row stays 0 because that table books the main session's own wall time.
decisions.why: A statement of what each table measures (FR-005 keeps the critical-path wall clock apart from summed agent-minutes, as the approved proposal asked), not a defect left: the fix is to page-session (agent) lines, and the first table never counted those.

decisions.summary: Lands after T167 and before any landing that reads 449's per-task time; tagged [perf] as measurement work, with no engine-speed checklist.
decisions.why: The GM 2026-11-20: 'this kind of measurement task [is] to be counted as a performance task for the purpose of scheduling and coming first'; the order follows the dependency on T167.

decisions.id: T168-7 tests written with the code
decisions.summary: No red run recorded; the tests assert the re-booked counts, untouched lines, the second run's 0, the dry run's unchanged bytes, the unlisted and task-less sessions, and a missing log's exit 1.
decisions.why: FR-012's red-first requirement covers the refusals of FR-006 to FR-009, FR-011 and FR-013; this is a correction tool, not one of those refusals, so no requirement of the spec is narrowed. Test discipline beyond that is not a fidelity question.

decisions.id: T168-8 backup before the real run
decisions.summary: The 449 log was backed up to .git/l7r-events/449-rust-codebase.jsonl.pre-t168 before the run.
decisions.why: An operational precaution; narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: Each of the nine hook entries in .claude/settings.json becomes "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/scripts/hooks/l7r-hook <event> (or setup); a new POSIX sh launcher does what the inline commands did (mirror's l7r-guard.sh first if executable, else the copy beside it; setup runs the mirror's setup-dev-env.sh --ensure else the tree's), with the commands' reasons moved into its header.
decisions.why: The 2026-11-23 amendment asks whether hooks can 'accomplish the same thing with no loss of fidelity and fewer tokens'. The harness prints the entry's command with every block or notice, so the command is part of the hook output the GM named; shortening it from 239-330 to 49-63 characters while keeping the mirror-first dispatcher choice, the events and the behavior (hand comparison: all nine identical) is exactly 'the same thing ... fewer tokens'.

decisions.summary: Timeouts (60/600/900 s, above the wrapper's 45 s build limit) and the status message stay as they are.
decisions.why: Preserves behavior, as 'no loss of fidelity' requires; decides nothing the request left open.

decisions.id: T169-D3 escape marker out of the commands
decisions.summary: The escape marker each command carried (so the guard-file guard would pass the settings edit) is dropped; the edit goes through make guard-edit and its reason into the guard log and commit message.
decisions.why: The marker was the permit mechanism, not information a hook message's reader needs; the guard-file guard still refuses an unpermitted settings edit, so enforcement is unchanged ('real enforcement', 2026-11-19) and only the repeated token cost goes.

decisions.id: T169-D4 launcher held as a guard file
decisions.summary: scripts/hooks/l7r-hook is added to guard_file_hooks.rs GUARD_SOURCE and make_only_hooks.rs GUARD_FILE/SOURCE_NAMES; named l7r-hook rather than run so make-only's substring screen does not walk most commands.
decisions.why: The launcher now decides what the settings decided, so holding it as the settings were held keeps the protection the old commands had - no loss of fidelity. The name is an implementation choice inside the request.

decisions.summary: workflow_hooks.rs replays a tree's settings commands with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR set to that tree, since the new command depends on it and a missing launcher would exit 127 and let a unit through unguarded.
decisions.why: A defect the change itself would introduce (a guard silently passing work, a wrong outcome), fixed in the same task; keeps behavior the same, as asked.

decisions.id: T169-D11 launcher resolved through CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR always
decisions.summary: The old command read CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR only when the mirror had no dispatcher; the new one always finds the launcher through it, so a session whose project directory lacks scripts/hooks/l7r-hook would run no hook.
decisions.why: The launcher lives in the same tree as the settings that name it, so any session loading these settings from a tree has it; the one consumer that ran settings against another tree (the wave replay) is fixed (D5), and page sessions are observed to run from the clone's root (pages/src/runner.rs current_dir(root)). The block shows no case where these settings load without the launcher, so no behavior is lost.

decisions.summary: The hooks suite gains a length case refusing any hook command over 64 characters (a knob, GUESS), plus an entry case requiring each entry to be the launcher and launcher cases.
decisions.why: A test whose only effect is to keep the requested shortening in place (delete the shortening and the check has nothing left to check) is enforcement of the request, not unrequested scope (GM 2026-09-20).

decisions.summary: make-only's GUARD_FILE alternative l7r-guard\.sh matched any name ending so and refused a Python write of tests/hooks/test-l7r-guard.sh; the dispatcher's and launcher's names become whole names, pinned by the left-alone case; the pattern's other alternatives were read for the same shape (method stated).
decisions.why: A check refusing good work is a defect (constitution XIV); fixing it as found, with the class searched and the method recorded, is fix-as-we-go, not a narrowing.

decisions.id: T169-D8 live-probe event lines left booked by fallback
decisions.summary: The two live claude -p probes left 18 lines in 449's event log booked to T341 and 4 in 451's booked to T168 by the clone's mark (fallback), about a minute of where-time; left as the cost of a live test, not a defect. The first probe's one escalation-check pass has its ledger row written by hand, so no landing refuses on it; the second left no review pass.
decisions.why: The fallback attribution worked as designed on an untagged session; a minute of probe noise is a difference no reader of where-time's report would act on, not a wrong outcome of a tool, so leaving it needs no ruling. The section states it as found-and-left with its measurement.

decisions.summary: Hand comparison of all nine old vs new commands (same stdout, stderr, exit), red-first suite and crate tests, two live sessions; SessionStart, setup and PostToolUseFailure, which print nothing on a healthy call, are covered by the hand comparison and suite rather than live.
decisions.why: Verification of the requested 'no loss of fidelity'; events that emit nothing cannot be observed live, so covering them by the hand comparison narrows nothing the request asked for.

decisions.summary: Classed as performance work under 451 FR-013 (the builders' loop), claimed in tokens, not time: per-call wall time is measured unchanged within noise.
decisions.why: The block claims a token saving, not a speed-up. That rests on request.md: the GM framed this amendment as a token cost (2026-11-23, 'That amount of output consumes tokens'), and the approved 2026-11-19 improvement 1 ties a builder's context size to its model calls' speed, so fewer stored characters per hook message serves the builders' loop FR-013 names. The scheduling label decides nothing the request left open.

decisions.summary: Measure which guard messages cost most (count x length), shorten the top ones keeping every fix command and escape, and hold every suite-rendered message to a budget and a content-keyed review instead of a per-hook comment
decisions.why: The GM asked for fewer tokens with no loss of fidelity, mechanically enforced, and asked 'What do you think?' about the comment form. A budget check plus a content-keyed review enforces the same thing mechanically and cannot drift from the text the way a comment can. Every new or changed wording is held to it.

decisions.summary: Mid-task notice in full once, then a 53-character line while unchanged; said in full again after a sync, a failed refresh or a SessionStart
decisions.why: Fewer tokens. A repeat carries no new information and the full text comes back whenever the state changes.

decisions.summary: A commit's notice gives the count, the first row and make ledger-owed for the rest, with the fix and LEDGER_ROWS_OK in full; history cut to the code comment
decisions.why: Fewer tokens. The command for the rest, the fix and the escape are all kept.

decisions.summary: Seven rewrite notices say what was done and what to do; the history moves to the code comment
decisions.why: Fewer tokens. The actionable content is kept.

decisions.summary: Notice trimmed from 278 to 248 characters
decisions.why: Fewer tokens.

decisions.summary: House-style notices put each word in a code span, so the record no longer trips the house-style delta check
decisions.why: A defect the work itself exposed (the push failed), fixed in the task. It costs a few characters.

decisions.summary: The record's head column is the start of the hashed wording, with paths, ids and numbers masked, and it never ends inside a code span
decisions.why: Keeps the enforcement record stable and keeps it passing the delta check. Fixes a defect the closing checks found.

decisions.id: D8 stored head masks relative paths (changed since CLEAR)
decisions.summary: Masks::stored masks relative paths in the head at the record's one write. Keys are unchanged. REHEAD=1 rewrote the 290 heads, the other columns did not change, and the test went red first
decisions.why: Fixes a defect found at landing: the preflight refused a head that carried a built research page's path. It changes neither which wordings are enforced nor their keys, so the request's enforcement is untouched. It narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: A list in a guard message shows its first two items and 'and N more:' with a command (or a kept file) that prints all of them, and the whole list wherever that is no longer. Eight list-growing wordings found by a stated census are capped and held at their worst case. Adds make crate-checks CRATE= and makes stale-terms print every candidate
decisions.why: Fewer tokens with no loss of fidelity: every item can still be reached in full by the named command, and the fix commands and escapes are kept. The census names its search space. The new target keeps FR-007's naming of each changed crate's checks.

decisions.summary: Every changed wording is reviewed by message-check through round 7. One BREVITY suggestion (BACKGROUNDED's clause) was not taken, and round 2 then passed that clause
decisions.why: This is the subagent review the GM asked for. Declining one cut keeps a piece of information the reader needs (no loss of fidelity), and the reviewer later passed it.

decisions.summary: NOTICE_BUDGET 900 and REFUSE_BUDGET 1,800, labeled GUESS and set from the longest rendered wordings rounded up
decisions.why: The mechanical limit the request implies. The knobs are labeled and measured.

decisions.summary: Left unshortened here: finished-run's detached-run block (3), the set-down blocks (4, 7, 10, T171's), review-round's long refusal (8, seen twice), the persisted context (9, not a guard message whose source is named), and finished-run's Stop notices (they never reach the model)
decisions.why: Each has a measured reason: each run's text is distinct, the work belongs to another task, it was seen twice, or it costs nothing. None is a wrong outcome left in place.

decisions.id: D13 255 wordings baselined unreviewed, filed T177
decisions.summary: Wordings that stood before T170 are marked BASELINE without review. The pop-ups' batch refusal and set-down's blocks are not held at their worst case. T177 is filed as the next performance work, before T22
decisions.why: The enforcement the GM asked for exists and holds every new or changed wording. Each baselined wording is within budget and is one sessions already read today, so nothing is a wrong outcome. The rest of the review is a filed and ordered task in the same feature, not dropped. The pop-ups' list is its fix command's own argument, so capping it would lose fidelity.

decisions.summary: repo-safety, shell-check and source-block render nothing to the check, and the finished-run and set-down blocks bypass protocol::run, so the budget check does not hold them yet. T174 is filed after T170 and before T173
decisions.why: Reaching them needs each of those suites to drive the binary's hook path, which is outside T170's guards. The gap is measured (17 of 58 corpus files empty), named, filed and ordered in the same feature, so the mechanical enforcement is completed rather than given up.

decisions.summary: Runs after T169 and T171. T174 before T173. T177 before T22
decisions.why: Sequencing that follows FR-013's performance-first rule. Nothing the request asked for is removed.
